evidence: The Lam Rim scope idiom is 'skyes bu chung ngu' (person of lesser capacity); 'chung du' is not parsable here, since a terminative du cannot feed the comitative dang that follows. FILED AGAINST PROPOSAL B, WHICH REJECTED IT — B's counter-evidence does not survive checking. (1) Same-course parallel: C03:225 is the outline heading for this very section and reads 'skyes bu chung ngu dang thun mong ba'i lam gyi rim par blo sbyang ba' — identical to this clause word-for-word, including the distinctive 'rim par' (other witnesses read 'rim pa la'), differing ONLY in ngu/du. Its ACIP reads 'SKYES BU CHUNG NGU DANG ... RIM PAR BLO SBYANG BA,'. C03:401, the section header, glosses it 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'. (2) Counts: 'skyes bu chung ngu' occurs in 23 spine segments (C02:40, C08:309, C09:214, C09:216, C16:238, C17:402, TCS01:223, TCS01:317, TCS01:318, TCS03:20, SSL:107, SSL:111, SSL:395, ...); 'skyes bu chung du' occurs in exactly 2 — this segment and TCS18Commentary:322, a different text and not a parallel of this passage. (3) B's claim that 'chung du' is 'a live adverbial form' across TCS03/05/06/09/10/11/15/16 is a category error. I enumerated every 'chung du' in the spine with context: TCS03:446 'chung du song', TCS05:499 'mthu chung du gtang', TCS06:161 'chung du 'gro', TCS06:341 'chung chung du gnas', TCS07:681 'chung du 'gro', TCS09:501 'chung du 'gro', TCS10:322/418 'je chung je chung du bsdus/song', TCS10:323/405, TCS11:265/333, TCS15:448 'drod chung du 'gro', TCS16Reading:159, EM:956, EM:1126, C01:105 — every one is adverbial terminative du plus a verb of diminution ('become/make smaller'), a wholly different construction. Not one is the skyes-bu scope idiom. The string 'chung du dang' occurs exactly twice in the entire spine: this segment and TCS18Commentary:322. The true adverbial du never once feeds a comitative dang. (4) B read the ACIP apparatus backwards. In ACIP, {%X} is the EDITORS' CORRECTION, so GIE:650 "chung du'i {%ngu'i} chung du {%ngu}" is evidence that du-for-ngu IS an error, not that it is accepted; the same correction recurs at AK:156 'chung du {%ngu%}', AK:842 'chung dur {%ngur}', GK:97 'chung dus {%ngus}', SOS:25 'chung dus {%ngus}'. This is a documented, editor-corrected keying slip class. (5) The ACIP field of this same segment also reads 'CHUNG DU', so the slip is in the keyed source, not introduced by the wylie transliteration step. Span s402-21 preserves 'chung du' byte-for-byte per rule 1.
